::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 20th [1891-3]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Rosemary, Viscountess Chaplin
:::

Dear [Miss Cox](people/person_1642.qmd)
I cannot promise to vote for [Anne Fay](people/person_1679.qmd) but she interests me much, as I have seen a good deal of the same kind of illness and I will see whether it is possible.

I well remember the days of the Cardioscope, which I think was one of the best ideas [we](organizations/other_52.qmd) ever had.[^1]  I have now a [fellow Editor](people/person_329.qmd) who has taken the MSS especially of poetry.  I think she must have your verses

yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: ‘The Cardioscope’ was a series in *MP* (July-November 1851).  The idea was that an instrument could test the feelings of the human heart as a stethoscope does.  There is a volume of poems, 1887, by Agnes Cox. CMY is evidently being asked to cast a vote in favour of Anne Fay for admission to some hospital or almshouse.  There is a probable contributor called [Harriet Lucy Cox](people/person_375.qmd) (b. Waddesdon 1825/6) who later married the Rev. Arthur Baker (1817-1868) and transcribed books into Braille;  it is possible that she may have been the author of ‘The Cardioscope’, and a relation of this Miss Cox.
